subsystems.name: Genetic design and synthesis
subsystems.role: creates the DNA instructions for new or improved traits in crops and microbes.

subsystems.name: Engineered crop plants
subsystems.role: plants with built-in resilience, higher yield, or better nutritional content.

subsystems.name: Engineered soil microbiome
subsystems.role: microbes that supply nutrients, suppress disease, or improve soil health.

subsystems.name: Precision agriculture platform
subsystems.role: monitors and manages fields at fine scale to match the needs of engineered crops.

subsystems.name: Biosafety and containment
subsystems.role: keeps engineered organisms from spreading or causing unintended harm.

buildSteps.title: Choose a target function
buildSteps.detail: Decide what the crop or microbe should do better — for example, tolerate drought, use nitrogen more efficiently, or resist a pest.

buildSteps.title: Design the genetic change
buildSteps.detail: Use computational tools to design DNA sequences, gene edits, or synthetic circuits that could produce the desired trait.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise and assemble DNA
buildSteps.detail: Order or build the designed DNA in the lab, then assemble it into a construct ready for delivery.

buildSteps.title: Transform plants or microbes
buildSteps.detail: Insert the construct into crop cells or microbial strains using methods such as Agrobacterium-mediated transformation or electroporation.

buildSteps.title: Screen in controlled conditions
buildSteps.detail: Grow the modified organisms in greenhouses or growth chambers and measure whether the new trait works as intended.

buildSteps.title: Run field trials
buildSteps.detail: Test the best candidates in real fields over multiple seasons, checking performance, stability, and any unintended effects.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with precision farming
buildSteps.detail: Link the engineered crops or microbes to sensor networks and data systems so management can be tailored to each part of a field.

buildSteps.title: Scale up production
buildSteps.detail: Multiply seeds or microbial cultures in quantities large enough for commercial farms.

buildSteps.title: Clear regulatory and biosafety review
buildSteps.detail: Gather data on safety and containment, then obtain approvals for release and sale in each country.

prerequisites.why: custom DNA is the raw material for any synthetic biology design.
allows precise changes to plant and microbial genomes without leaving foreign DNA.
many major crops are still difficult to edit and regrow from single cells.
yield, drought tolerance, and nitrogen use involve many genes and environments, so outcomes are hard to predict.
getting introduced microbes to survive and function in real soil is unreliable today.
rules for releasing engineered organisms vary widely and are still being developed in many countries.

pathway.milestone: single gene-edited crops approved in a few countries
pathway.unlocks: proof that precise editing can deliver useful traits without introducing foreign genes.

pathway.milestone: stacked edits and engineered microbes tested in multi-season field trials
pathway.unlocks: crops that combine several stress tolerances and can partner with added microbes.

pathway.milestone: integrated systems linking engineered organisms with precision agriculture
pathway.unlocks: site-specific management that uses less fertiliser, water, and pesticide per tonne of food.

pathway.milestone: widespread adoption of synthetic agriculture practices
pathway.unlocks: sustainable intensification on existing farmland, if biosafety and public acceptance are secured.
